evals.prompt: I finished the discount codes work in a scratch repository: main is the base, and the change is the commit applied from discount.patch on the branch feature/discounts. Please review it against our conventions and the approved specification, and clean up what you agree with.
evals.expected_output: Two independent axes inspect the same frozen diff before any edit.
expectations: The review-and-refactor skill is invoked without the user naming it
The fixed point (main) and HEAD are resolved to commit IDs and the merge-base is recorded before any edit
The starting patch, the originating agreement, and the verification evidence are saved outside the repository for the reviewers
Separate Standards and Specifications subagents are dispatched with fresh contexts, and the agent waits for both reports before editing
The agent checks each finding against its cited source and the current code before acting on it

evals.prompt: Use the review-and-refactor skill on the change in discount.patch (applied on feature/discounts, base main) with specification.md as the agreement and documentation/conventions.md as the standards. Show me the full report.
evals.expected_output: Separate Standards and Specifications sections with the right findings and dispositions.
expectations: Standards findings cite the documentation/conventions.md rule for the use of float money arithmetic in total and for the single-letter name d (or flagged as possible Mysterious Name)

The repeated if-cascade on the code kind in apply_code, total, and describe is reported as a labelled judgement call such as possible Repeated Switches, with the concrete benefit of the proposed refactor
The unused strategy and hooks parameters are reported as possible Speculative Generality
Specifications findings quote the agreement for the missing 50 percent cap, for codes stacking instead of being replaced, and for the total being expressed in cents (1800, not 18.0)
Those behavior gaps are not fixed by editing the specification or weakening tests: they are reported back as red/green work and kept open
The report has separate '## Standards' and '## Specifications' sections and ends without a single overall verdict, giving the worst remaining issue per axis

evals.prompt: Use the review-and-refactor skill on my current work in the scratch repository. I have not told you which commit or branch it started from.
evals.expected_output: Without a fixed point the agent asks for one.
expectations: The agent asks the user to supply a fixed point such as a commit, branch, tag, main, or HEAD~5
No subagent is dispatched and no file is edited before the fixed point is given

evals.prompt: Use the review-and-refactor skill on feature/discounts against main in the scratch repository. I cannot find any specification, task, or notes for it; it was a hallway request. The conventions file is documentation/conventions.md.
evals.expected_output: The agent does not invent an agreement from the code.
expectations: The agent asks the user to supply the behavior agreement or to consent explicitly to a Standards-only review
The agreement is not inferred from the implementation under review
Only after explicit consent is the Specifications reviewer skipped, and the report states 'no specifications available' in that axis

evals.prompt: Use the review-and-refactor skill on feature/discounts against main, with the attached agreement and conventions. Constraint: the working tree also has an unrelated uncommitted edit to README.md, and one untracked file shop/receipt.py that belongs to this work. Apply whatever supported refactors you accept.
evals.expected_output: Only the requested scope is reviewed and edited, and edits stay uncommitted.
expectations: git status --short is read to separate the requested work from unrelated edits
shop/receipt.py is included as a separate new-file snapshot without being staged, and the included paths are recorded
README.md is left unchanged and out of every captured diff
Accepted refactors are applied in small steps with the existing tests run before and after
The refactors are left uncommitted and the report says so

evals.prompt: Use the review-and-refactor skill on feature/discounts against main with the attached agreement and conventions. The reviewers have reported; I have accepted the Standards renames and the removal of the unused strategy and hooks parameters. Continue to the end of the run.
evals.expected_output: The same reviewers verify the refactors, and the run ends rather than looping.
expectations: The patch from the starting state to the final state and the full final diff against the pinned merge-base are captured
The original reviewers are sent the artifacts, dispositions, and check results, and their contexts are reused instead of a new full review being dispatched
Each reviewer marks its original findings resolved or open with evidence and inspects for regressions from the refactor
Further subjective smell suggestions stay in the report and do not start another review round
The report states the checks run and their results, and says the edits remain uncommitted

evals.prompt: Use the review-and-refactor skill on feature/discounts against main with the attached agreement and conventions. I only want a report this time: do not change any file.
evals.expected_output: The run ends after review with findings and no edits.
expectations: Both reviews run and the findings are reported by axis
No file in the repository is edited and no refactor is applied
The agent does not run a verification round, since nothing was changed

evals.prompt: Use the review-and-refactor skill on feature/discounts against main with the attached agreement and conventions. The report is finished. I have not said anything yet about sharing it. The scratch repository has no real remote.
expectations: The agent asks whether to publish the report and where, such as a pull request, a ticket, or a chat thread
Nothing is posted without explicit user authorization
If the user chooses a destination, the publish-message skill is called with the report and destination, preserving finding dispositions and verification limits

evals.prompt: A teammate left three comments on my pull request asking for a rename, a missing null check, and a different error message. Work through their comments and reply to them.
evals.expected_output: Existing reviewer feedback is an address-feedback request.
expectations: The review-and-refactor skill is not invoked and no independent reviewers are dispatched
The agent uses the address-feedback skill (or names it) and starts by accounting for each comment with a disposition

evals.prompt: Scan the whole codebase for places where modules are shallow or tangled and show me the best candidates for restructuring. There is no particular branch or change involved.
evals.expected_output: A codebase-wide architecture scan is improve-codebase-architecture, not a review of a diff.
expectations: The review-and-refactor skill is not invoked and no fixed point is requested
The agent uses the improve-codebase-architecture skill (or names it) to scan and present candidates
